triples.rationale: Both oracles report a message from the Lord sent among the nations, calling them to rise for war against Idumea. The shared summons and named nation connect the two announcements.
triples.source_text: The vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord God to Idumea: I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent a dispatch to the nations: “Rise up! Let us rise against her for battle!”

target_units.text: I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent messengers to the nations: Gather and come against her; rise for war!

triples.rationale: Obadiah announces that Idumea has been made insignificant and dishonored among the nations. Jeremiah likewise describes her as made small among nations and despised among people.
triples.source_text: Look, I have made you insignificant among the nations; you are greatly dishonored.

target_units.text: I made you small among nations, easily despised among people.

triples.rationale: Both Idumea oracles connect the heart's pride or insolence with holes in rocks and an elevated position. Obadiah voices the inhabitant's boast as a question about who can bring him down. Jeremiah announces that the Lord will bring the addressee down despite the elevated eagle's nest.
triples.source_text: The pride of your heart has lifted you up, you who camp in holes in the rocks, raising his dwelling high and saying in his heart, “Who will bring me down to the ground?”

target_units.text: Your playfulness assailed you; your heart’s insolence destroyed holes in rocks and seized the strength of a high hill. For he raised his nest like an eagle; from there I will bring you down.

triples.rationale: Obadiah describes soaring like an eagle and placing a nest among the stars, then announces that the Lord will bring the addressee down from there. Jeremiah likewise joins the elevated eagle's nest with the Lord bringing the addressee down.
triples.source_text: If you soar like an eagle, and if you place your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says the Lord.

target_units.text: Your playfulness assailed you; your heart’s insolence destroyed holes in rocks and seized the strength of a high hill. For he raised his nest like an eagle; from there I will bring you down.

triples.rationale: Both passages compare Idumea's loss with grape gatherers and thieves at night. Obadiah asks whether ordinary gatherers would leave a gleaning; Jeremiah announces gatherers who leave no remnants, sharpening the devastation described by the shared imagery.
triples.source_text: If thieves came in to you, or robbers by night, where would you have been cast away? Would they not have stolen enough for themselves? And if grape gatherers came in to you, would they not have left a gleaning?

target_units.text: For grape gatherers came to you; they will leave you no remnants. Like thieves by night they will lay their hand upon you.

triples.rationale: Obadiah describes Esau searched out and his hidden things seized. Jeremiah likewise names Esau, then says their secrets are uncovered and they cannot hide, preserving that passage's change to plural pronouns.
triples.source_text: How Esau has been searched out, and his hidden things seized!

target_units.text: For I dragged Esau away and uncovered their secrets; they certainly cannot hide. They perished by the hand of his brother and his neighbor, and it is not possible

triples.rationale: Obadiah's covenant partners and men at peace become opponents and set ambushes. The psalm similarly laments treachery from a trusted man of peace, presenting the reversal of an expected peaceful relationship.
triples.source_text: All the men of your covenant sent you out as far as your borders; the men at peace with you opposed you and prevailed over you. They set ambushes beneath you. There is no understanding in them.

target_units.text: For even the man of my peace, in whom I hoped, who ate my loaves, magnified treachery against me.

triples.relationship: parallel loss of the wise and their counsel
triples.rationale: Obadiah announces destruction of the wise out of Idumea and understanding out of Mount Esau. Jeremiah's Idumea oracle addresses the loss of wisdom in Teman and counsel among the discerning.
triples.source_text: On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the wise from Idumea and understanding from Mount Esau.

target_units.text: For Idumea, thus says the Lord: There is no longer wisdom in Teman; counsel perished from the discerning; their wisdom went away.

triples.rationale: Obadiah describes Teman's warriors terrified so that a person may be removed from Mount Esau. Jeremiah joins judgment concerning Teman with Idumea's strong men's hearts becoming like the heart of a woman in labor.
triples.source_text: Your warriors from Teman will be terrified, so that a person may be removed from Mount Esau,

target_units.text: Therefore hear the Lord’s counsel that He planned against Idumea and His purpose against Teman’s inhabitants: Surely the smallest sheep will be swept together; surely their dwelling will be made untrodden over her.
For at the sound of their fall the earth shook, and your cry was heard at the sea.
Like an eagle he will look and stretch his wings over her fortifications. That day Idumea’s strong men’s hearts will be like the heart of a woman in labor.

triples.rationale: Obadiah condemns violence and impiety toward the brother Jacob. Deuteronomy explicitly forbids abhorring an Edomite because he is a brother, making the kinship obligation relevant to the violence condemned here.
triples.source_text: because of the slaughter and the impiety toward your brother Jacob; and shame will cover you, and you will be removed forever.

target_units.text: You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother; you shall not abhor an Egyptian, for you were a resident alien in his land.

triples.relationship: parallel judgment for violence against Judah
triples.rationale: Obadiah gives slaughter and impiety toward Jacob as the reason for Esau's shame and removal. Ezekiel similarly grounds judgment on Idumea in its vengeance and grudge against Judah's house.
triples.source_text: because of the slaughter and the impiety toward your brother Jacob; and shame will cover you, and you will be removed forever.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: Because Idumea acted in vengeance against Judah’s house, and they bore a grudge and exacted punishment,
therefore thus says the Lord: I will stretch My hand against Idumea and utterly destroy human and animal from her. I will make her a wilderness, and those pursued from Thaiman will fall by the sword.
I will place My vengeance upon Idumea by the hand of My people Israel. They will act in Idumea according to My anger and My wrath, and they will recognize My vengeance, says the Lord.

triples.rationale: Obadiah condemns the slaughter of Jacob by his brother. Joel specifically announces Idumea's desolation because of injustice toward Judah's sons and the shedding of righteous blood.
triples.source_text: because of the slaughter and the impiety toward your brother Jacob; and shame will cover you, and you will be removed forever.

target_units.text: Egypt will become desolate, and Idumea a desolate plain, because of injustices concerning the sons of Judah, because they poured out righteous blood in their land.

triples.rationale: Obadiah places Esau alongside foreigners who enter Jerusalem's gates and take its strength. The psalm remembers Edom's sons urging Jerusalem's destruction down to its foundations, likewise treating them as participants in her calamity.
triples.source_text: From the day you stood opposed, on the day foreigners took his strength captive and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.

target_units.text: Remember, Lord, Edom’s sons on Jerusalem’s day, those saying, “Empty her, empty her, down to the foundation within her!”

triples.relationship: parallel accusation of dispossession and lots
triples.rationale: Obadiah describes foreigners taking strength captive and casting lots over Jerusalem. Joel presents the Lord judging the nations over scattered Israel, the division of His land and lots cast over His people.
triples.source_text: From the day you stood opposed, on the day foreigners took his strength captive and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.

target_units.text: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them over My people and My inheritance Israel, who were scattered among the nations; and they divided up My land
and cast lots over My people; they gave the boys to prostitutes and sold the girls for wine, which they drank.

triples.relationship: shared prohibition of rejoicing at another's fall
triples.rationale: Obadiah forbids rejoicing and boasting over Judah's destruction and affliction. Proverbs likewise forbids rejoicing when even an enemy falls, explaining that such delight displeases the Lord.
triples.source_text: Do not look on your brother’s day, on the day of strangers; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not speak boastfully on the day of affliction.

target_units.text: If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and at his tripping do not lift yourself up,
for the Lord will see, and it will not please Him, and He will turn His wrath away from him.

triples.relationship: parallel condemnation of exploiting Israel's ruin
triples.rationale: Obadiah forbids entering the afflicted people's gates and joining attacks on their strength. Ezekiel condemns Mount Seir for claiming the two countries and treating Israel's desolate mountains as food, describing another form of exploitation of Israel's calamity.
triples.source_text: Do not enter the gates of peoples on the day of their suffering. You, too, must not look on their assembly on the day of their destruction, and do not join in attacking their strength on the day of their destruction.

target_units.text: Because you said, “The two nations and the two countries will be mine, and I will inherit them,” and the Lord is there,
therefore, I live, says the Lord: I will deal with you according to your hostility and make Myself known to you when I judge you.
You will know that I am the Lord. I heard the voice of your blasphemies, because you said, “Israel’s mountains are desolate; they have been given to us for food.”
You spoke grandly against Me with your mouth. I heard.

triples.rationale: Obadiah forbids blocking escape routes to destroy or confine fugitives. Ezekiel accuses Mount Seir of treacherously ambushing Israel's house with the sword; both condemn violence directed at Israel in its distress.
triples.source_text: Do not stand at their escape routes to destroy those of them who are being saved, and do not shut in those fleeing from them on the day of affliction.

target_units.text: Because you became an everlasting enemy and ambushed Israel’s house treacherously, by enemies’ hand, with a sword at the final time of injustice,

triples.relationship: parallel repayment upon the aggressor's head
triples.rationale: Obadiah announces that a nation's own actions will be repaid upon its head. Joel uses that same repayment language when condemning the seizure of treasures and the sale of Judah's people.
triples.source_text: For the day of the Lord is near against all the nations. Just as you acted, so it will be for you; your recompense will be repaid upon your own head.

target_units.text: What have you to do with Me, Tyre and Sidon and all Galilee of foreigners? Are you repaying Me a recompense? Or do you bear a sharp grudge against Me? I will speedily repay your recompense upon your heads,
because you took My silver and gold and brought My chosen and beautiful things into your temples,
and sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, so as to thrust them out of their own borders.
Look, I am rousing them from the place to which you sold them, and I will repay your recompense upon your heads,

triples.rationale: Obadiah moves from drinking on the holy mountain to the nations drinking and going down. In the Jeremiah account, the nations receive the Lord's wine cup of judgment, with Jerusalem and Judah heading the listed recipients. Both connect the city's judgment with that of the nations; Jeremiah explicitly names the cup.
triples.source_text: For just as you drank on My holy mountain, all the nations will drink wine; they will drink and go down, and they will be as though they did not exist.

target_units.text: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Take this cup of unmixed wine from My hand, and give it to all the nations to whom I send you to drink,
and they will drink, vomit, and go mad before the sword I am sending among them.
And I took the cup from the Lord’s hand and gave it to the nations to whom the Lord sent me to drink:
Jerusalem, Judah’s cities, Judah’s kings, and its rulers, to make them a desolation, an untrodden place, and a hissing;

triples.rationale: Obadiah locates salvation on Mount Zion. Joel likewise locates escape on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem within the promise that those calling on the Lord's name will be saved.
triples.source_text: But on Mount Zion there will be salvation, and it will be holy; the house of Jacob will possess those who possessed them.

target_units.text: Everyone who calls upon the Lord’s name will be saved, for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be one who escapes, as the Lord said, and bearers of good news whom the Lord has called.”

triples.rationale: Obadiah says Mount Zion will be holy as Jacob receives possession. Joel presents the Lord dwelling on His holy mountain and Jerusalem becoming a holy city, sharing the restoration's holiness setting.
triples.source_text: But on Mount Zion there will be salvation, and it will be holy; the house of Jacob will possess those who possessed them.

target_units.text: You will recognize that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Zion on My holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy city, and foreigners will no longer pass through her.

triples.relationship: Israel as the agent of judgment on Idumea
triples.rationale: Obadiah pictures Jacob and Joseph as fire consuming Esau's stubble. Ezekiel states that the Lord will place His vengeance on Idumea by the hand of His people Israel; both place Israel in the role of executing that judgment.
triples.source_text: The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will blaze against them and consume them, and there will be no bearer of fire in the house of Esau, because the Lord has spoken.

target_units.text: I will place My vengeance upon Idumea by the hand of My people Israel. They will act in Idumea according to My anger and My wrath, and they will recognize My vengeance, says the Lord.

triples.relationship: parallel inheritance of Edom by Jacob
triples.rationale: Obadiah includes possession of Esau's mountain in Israel's future holdings. Balaam's oracle likewise calls Edom and Esau an inheritance and speaks of one arising from Jacob.
triples.source_text: Those in the Negeb will possess the mountain of Esau, and those in the Shephelah will possess the foreigners. They will possess the mountain of Ephraim, the plain of Samaria, Benjamin and the land of Gilead.

target_units.text: And Edom shall become an inheritance, and Esau, his enemy, shall become an inheritance; Israel acted with strength.
And one shall arise from Jacob and destroy whoever escapes from a city.

triples.rationale: Obadiah promises possession of Esau's mountain and further territories. Ezekiel records Mount Seir's claim to possess the two countries and Israel's desolate mountains; the passages present opposing claims and a reversal of who will possess the land.
triples.source_text: Those in the Negeb will possess the mountain of Esau, and those in the Shephelah will possess the foreigners. They will possess the mountain of Ephraim, the plain of Samaria, Benjamin and the land of Gilead.

target_units.text: Because you said, “The two nations and the two countries will be mine, and I will inherit them,” and the Lord is there,
therefore, I live, says the Lord: I will deal with you according to your hostility and make Myself known to you when I judge you.
You will know that I am the Lord. I heard the voice of your blasphemies, because you said, “Israel’s mountains are desolate; they have been given to us for food.”

triples.rationale: Obadiah links Jerusalem's deportation with future inheritance of cities in the Negeb. Jeremiah promises renewed acquisition of fields, explicitly including the Negeb's cities, because the Lord will bring back the exiles. The connection concerns restored possession rather than identifying Obadiah's Ephrathah with another place.
triples.source_text: And this is the beginning of the deportation: for the sons of Israel, the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and the deportation of Jerusalem as far as Ephrathah. They will inherit the cities of the Negeb.

target_units.text: Fields will again be acquired in the land of which you say, It is untrodden by people and animals, and they were handed over to the Chaldeans.

They will acquire fields with silver, and you will write a document, seal it, and call witnesses in Benjamin’s land, around Jerusalem, in Judah’s cities, the hill-country cities, the cities of the Shephelah, and the cities of the Negeb, because I will bring back their exiles.

triples.relationship: parallel judgment on Esau through God's people
triples.rationale: Obadiah describes saved men ascending from Zion to execute judgment on Esau's mountain. Ezekiel similarly says the Lord's vengeance on Idumea will be carried out by His people Israel.
triples.source_text: And men who have been saved shall ascend from Mount Zion to execute judgment upon the mountain of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.

target_units.text: I will place My vengeance upon Idumea by the hand of My people Israel. They will act in Idumea according to My anger and My wrath, and they will recognize My vengeance, says the Lord.

triples.relationship: shared kingship of the Lord over the nations
triples.rationale: Obadiah concludes that the kingdom will belong to the Lord after judgment on Esau. The psalm declares that kingship belongs to the Lord and that He rules the nations, setting the individual oracle within that wider sovereignty.
triples.source_text: And men who have been saved shall ascend from Mount Zion to execute judgment upon the mountain of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.

target_units.text: All the limits of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations will bow down before Thee,
because kingship belongs to the Lord, and He is master of the nations.
